main.job: explanatory mode: presents a statement as background or explanation, or asks for one
main.why: Everywhere in speech; without it learners sound blunt or miss that someone is asking 'what's going on?'

main.job: humble 'I (humbly) do X', the business and announcement register
main.why: Politeness is grammatical in Japanese; this is the most frequent humble frame in work, shops and announcements

main.job: partial negation: 'it's not that…', softening or correcting an inference
main.why: Very common hedge; learners read it as a full negative and misunderstand

main.job: announce your own decision to do something
main.why: Core decision construction; half of a pair that is constantly confused

main.job: report an outcome decided by others or by circumstances
main.why: Used for transfers, schedules, rules; signals the speaker didn't decide alone
Constant in casual speech as ちゃう/じゃう; blocks understanding if missed

main.job: contrary-to-expectation link with frustration or disappointment ('even though… and yet')
main.why: Carries emotional tone English speakers miss; not the same as けど

main.job: 'as I thought / after all': confirms or reverses back to an expectation
main.why: One of the most frequent discourse words in spoken Japanese

main.job: expectation based on reasoning: 'should be / is supposed to'
main.why: Distinct from べき and でしょう; key for plans and reasoning

main.job: brush-off: 'not particularly / nothing much', often dismissive
main.why: High-frequency reply with a register trap (can sound curt)

main.job: tentative impression: 'I get the feeling that…'
main.why: Main way to hedge opinions in conversation

main.job: hedge: 'just in case / sort of, for now'
main.why: Extremely frequent; English speakers misread it as 'once'

spares.job: 'not necessarily': denies that something always holds
'considering…': result differs from what the premise suggests
spares.why: Frequent in reviews and small talk

spares.job: 'as expected of…': praise that confirms reputation

sets.name: こと + する/なる decision pair

shape.notes: B2 bare slice: per R-SEL-06 the basic building blocks (copula, existence, particles, questions, core verbs) are the B2 learner's floor; this list claims the constructions, register and discourse glue that still block fluent understanding. No closed set touched except the ことにする/ことになる pair, included whole. Sentence-final particles (よ/ね/よね) deliberately avoided so as not to start an open-ended set.
